title: Why does my breaker keep tripping?
excerpt: A breaker that trips is doing its job. Here's how to find out why, and when to stop resetting it and call us.
content:
A breaker trips to stop a circuit from overheating. Resetting it once is fine. Resetting it every day means something is wrong, and the breaker is the only thing standing between that fault and your walls.

1. Too much on one circuit

The most common cause. A space heater, a hair dryer and a kettle on the same kitchen or bathroom circuit can draw more than it's made for. Move one of them to another room and see if the tripping stops.

2. A worn outlet or appliance

Unplug everything on the circuit, reset the breaker, then plug things back in one at a time. If it trips when one appliance goes in, that appliance is the problem.

3. Damp or a loose connection

If it trips with nothing plugged in, or after rain, there's a fault in the wiring itself. That needs an electrician.

When to call straight away

  • The breaker trips again as soon as you reset it
  • You smell burning, or an outlet or switch is warm
  • You see scorch marks or hear buzzing from the panel

Any of those? Switch the circuit off and book a visit, or call us now. Our $79 diagnostic visit comes off the repair.

title: Is your home ready for an EV charger?
excerpt: Most homes can take a Level 2 charger without a panel upgrade. Three quick checks tell you where you stand.
content:
A Level 2 charger adds 25 to 30 miles of range an hour, so the car is full every morning. Before you buy one, three checks tell you what the install will involve.

Check your panel's size

Open the panel door and look at the main breaker at the top. 200 amps is the norm for newer homes and almost always has room. 100 amps can work, but we'll need to check the load first.

Look for space

A charger needs a double-width space for its breaker. If your panel is full, a tandem breaker or a small subpanel often solves it without a full upgrade.

Measure the distance

The closer the panel is to where you park, the cheaper the install. Garages next to the panel are the easiest; a charger at the end of a long driveway costs more.

Send us a photo of your panel when you book a visit and we can often price the job before we arrive. And ask about our $200 off EV charger installs.

title: Five signs your electrical panel needs replacing
excerpt: Panels last 25 to 40 years. If yours shows any of these signs, it's time for a check.
content:
Your panel is the heart of the house's wiring, and it's easy to forget about until something goes wrong. Here are the signs we look for.

  • It's a fuse box. Fuses aren't dangerous in themselves, but most fuse boxes are 60 years old and too small for modern homes.
  • It's a brand known to fail. Federal Pacific Stab-Lok and Zinsco panels can fail to trip in a fault.
  • It's warm, buzzing or smells hot. Switch off what you can and call us now.
  • Breakers trip often, or the lights dim when the air conditioning starts.
  • There's no room left for the new circuits you want.

We check your panel free with any visit. If it needs replacing, a panel upgrade usually takes a single day.

title: How to light a kitchen in three layers
excerpt: One light in the middle of the ceiling leaves you working in your own shadow. Here's the three-layer plan we use.
content:
Kitchens need more light than any other room, and from more directions. We plan them in three layers.

1. General light

Recessed LED downlights in a grid, about four feet apart, give even light across the room. Put them on a dimmer.

2. Task light

Under-cabinet strips light the counters where you chop and read recipes, without your head in the way. This is the layer most kitchens are missing.

3. Accent light

Pendants over an island or table make the room feel finished. Hang them 30 to 36 inches above the counter.

Want a plan for your kitchen? Book a visit and we'll walk the room with you. See our lighting service for prices.
